### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**1** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **177** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 33a0d4fa625cdfb69873a89a1e0f5d9f49fea744` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `db454817ef68a0b923e8fc6682f61f23c7fb6622` — the merge of head `608f5a6b90ac1b0c57d92b2121fee1d4ff5c02c2` into base `33a0d4fa625cdfb69873a89a1e0f5d9f49fea744`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin db454817ef68a0b923e8fc6682f61f23c7fb6622 && git checkout db454817ef68a0b923e8fc6682f61f23c7fb6622
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 33a0d4fa625cdfb69873a89a1e0f5d9f49fea744 608f5a6b90ac1b0c57d92b2121fee1d4ff5c02c2 && git checkout -B drift-repro 33a0d4fa625cdfb69873a89a1e0f5d9f49fea744 && git merge --no-ff 608f5a6b90ac1b0c57d92b2121fee1d4ff5c02c2

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 33a0d4fa625cdfb69873a89a1e0f5d9f49fea744
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.

Scope: packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/19.chart-series-measure-format-carrier-refused.ts (the published-schema hit), ui/packages/types/src/zod/data-display.zod.ts, ui/packages/types/src/data-display.ts, ui/packages/types/src/__tests__/chart-series-aggregate-refusal-11681.test.ts + read, not reviewed: ui/packages/types/src/zod/tombstone.zod.ts, ui/packages/types/src/zod/objectql.zod.ts, ui/packages/plugin-charts/src/normalizeChartSchema.ts, ui/packages/plugin-charts/src/AdvancedChartImpl.tsx, ui/packages/plugin-charts/src/ObjectChart.tsx, ui/packages/plugin-dashboard/src/DatasetWidget.tsx, ui/packages/plugin-report/src/DatasetReportRenderer.tsx, packages/spec/src/ui/chart.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/types.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/README.md

### ① Derived judgments

- Accept set, zod face — NARROWED, right. `ChartDataSeriesSchema` is a `z.looseObject`; on the base an authored `series[].measureFormat` is undeclared, kept in the parse output and handed on. The diff declares it as `retirementTombstone(...)`, which is `z.never({ error }).optional().describe(...)`: any value other than `undefined` is refused with one `invalid_type` issue at the key's own path, and the series array carries it to `series.N.measureFormat` on `ChartSchema`. Nothing else on the object changes; the `aggregate` arm is untouched and still refuses beside it.
- Accept set, TS face — right. `ChartDataSeries` gains `measureFormat?: never`. The interface has no index signature, so a fresh literal already failed the excess-property check; the member now also refuses a non-fresh object and gives the zod mirror a twin, which the mirror-parity ledger needs.
- Public surface — one new declared, unwritable member on each face (`ChartDataSeries.measureFormat`, `ChartDataSeriesSchema.shape.measureFormat`, and through it the generated JSON-Schema description). No export added or removed.
- Spec migration registry — one new D3 entry, `chart-series-measure-format-carrier-refused`, in `MIGRATIONS_BY_MAJOR[19].semantic`. The filename is derived from the id as `entries/README.md` requires, the five required `SemanticMigration` fields are present, and no `conversionIds` is claimed, which is right: there is no D2 conversion.
- Not changed, and rightly so: `@objectstack/spec` `ChartSeriesSchema` (a `strictObject` that never declared the key), the renderer's reader (`normalizeSeries` in `normalizeChartSchema.ts`), and the two producers.
- Pins — the harness covers what the card's acceptance names: three carrier shapes each refused with one issue naming the key, the node-level path, both keys refused together, a parsing control, the type-level `Eq` pins on both faces, and the `@ts-expect-error` literal. The literal pin alone would hold without the twin (excess-property check); the `Eq` pin on the twin is the one that binds it.

### ② Semver level

- Clause-②: `yes (narrowing)` — judged right. The direction is a narrowing of a published accept set (BREAKING), and each face gains a declared member. The line is at line start in the PR body, the changeset and the claim comment, and matches the card's seat ruling.
- `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` — right: a key a metadata author could write is now refused.
- Level — `@object-ui/types` minor and `@objectstack/spec` minor. AGENTS.md step 3: a kind other than `none` takes at least minor on each package the diff moves; the diff moves exactly these two (the tombstone and twin; the ledger entry). The precedent `.changeset/pre/35827-data-table-staged-edit-retired.md` has the same shape. Right.
- The changeset carries the BREAKING banner, a FROM → TO row, the one-line fix and exactly one `adr-0087: registered` marker whose id matches the entry. The PR title carries `!`. `Skills-docs: none` with its reason is present. `Check Changeset` is green on this head.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: empty in the os-dev-report. Nothing to answer.
- Dev flag, `out_of_scope_findings`: "the chart renderer still reads `measureFormat` off any raw node it is handed". Answered: by design. `normalizeSeries` must keep reading the key or the report and dashboard producers lose the axis units #37053 delivered; the card's target is the authoring faces. No escalation.
- Dev flag: the a4-U prepared patch did not arrive by the claim's cut-off, so the fix was written from the card. Answered: the diff is judged on its own tree, and it matches the card's "Shape of the fix".
- Reviewer's flag, outside this card's surface — read in code, not run: the `object-chart` node's INTERNAL series arm (`ui/packages/types/src/zod/objectql.zod.ts`, the `z.looseObject({ dataKey, ... })` arm of `series`) declares neither `aggregate` nor `measureFormat`, so it keeps both, and `ObjectChart.tsx` spreads the schema's `series` on to `ChartRenderer`. The same carrier is therefore still writable through that node. It predates this PR, `aggregate` has the same door, and the card names the static `chart` node only, so it is not a finding on this diff. It is a candidate follow-up card for the lane.
- SQL push-down: not applicable. The diff adds no query, no id materialisation and no in-app join.
- Head: this record covers `58dedb3e`. While it was being written the PR head moved to `608f5a6b` (a merge of main, 137 files, none of them one of this PR's five paths). The record does not cover that head.

### ④ Design judgment

The narrowing, against the published spec on main: `@objectstack/spec` `ChartSeriesSchema` is a strict object that has never declared `measureFormat`, and the only `percentScale` the spec declares is on the analytics answer's `fields[]`, not on any chart authoring shape. PR #37194 introduced the key as producer-filled and renderer-internal. So no declared capability is taken away at the consumer: the mirror's loose object accepted, by accident of being non-strict, a key the spec already refuses, and this diff makes that refusal real on the mirror, in the posture `aggregate` already has. The design holds.

Attempts to break it:

- Producers refused by their own schema? No. `DatasetWidget.tsx` and `DatasetReportRenderer.tsx` build series objects in code and hand them to the renderer; neither parses through `ChartSchema`. `Type Check UI`, `Test UI` and `Live E2E UI` are green on this head, so the `?: never` twin does not catch a producer either.
- "The axis `format` takes precedence over the carrier" — true as cited: `AdvancedChartImpl.tsx` `valueAxisTickFormatter` tries `formatterFor(axis.format)` first, then `measureTickFormatter(sharedMeasureFormat(...))`, then the compact default.
- The offered authored channel exists and parses: `ChartSchema.yAxis` is an array of the spec's `ChartAxisSchema`, whose `format` is declared; the harness pins a control.
- Ledger entry against its first consumer, `os migrate meta`: surface, replacement, reason and acceptance criteria describe this diff and nothing wider; the claim "no D2 conversion" is honest, since the carrier's facts have no one-to-one authored key.
- Both keys written together: refused at both paths; pinned.

Findings:

- N1 (nit) — the guidance says "to format this chart's value axis, write the axis `format`" without its limit. `formatterFor` reads a `%` pattern as a 0–1 fraction and knows five currency symbols, so the axis `format` cannot say what `percentScale: 'whole'` or an ISO code such as `CNY` said in the carrier; `normalizeChartSchema.ts` states this itself in the `measureTickFormatter` docblock. A static chart's rows are authored inline, so the author can store the fraction, and the axis behaviour is unchanged by this PR; the refusal and the contract are unaffected. The sentence appears in the tombstone string, the TS docblock, the ledger entry and the changeset. One clause in the changeset is enough ("a `%` pattern reads the value as a 0–1 fraction"); the code strings are an accepted deviation or a follow-up card.
- N2 (nit) — the changeset's FROM → TO row starts from `currency: 'CNY'` and ends at `format: '$0,0'`, which `formatterFor` prints as US dollars. `'¥0,0'` is the matching pattern. Prose face only.

No must-fix, no should-fix.
